Astrophys."],"published-print":{"date-parts":[[2021,9,8]]},"abstract":"<jats:p>The spin of a black hole is an important quantity to study, providing a window into the processes by which a black hole was born and grew. Furthermore, spin can be a potent energy source for powering relativistic jets and energetic particle acceleration. In this review, I describe the techniques currently used to detect and measure the spins of black holes. It is shown that: \u25aa\u2002 Two well-understood techniques, X-ray reflection spectroscopy and thermal continuum fitting, can be used to measure the spins of black holes that are accreting at moderate rates. There is a rich set of other electromagnetic techniques allowing us to extend spin measurements to lower accretion rates. \u25aa\u2002 Many accreting supermassive black holes are found to be rapidly spinning, although a population of more slowly spinning black holes emerges at masses above [Formula: see text] as expected from recent structure formation models. \u25aa\u2002 Many accreting stellar-mass black holes in X-ray binary systems are rapidly spinning and must have been born in this state. \u25aa\u2002 The advent of gravitational wave astronomy has enabled the detection of spin effects in merging binary black holes. Most of the premerger black holes are found to be slowly spinning, a notable exception being an object that may itself be a merger product. \u25aa\u2002 The stark difference in spins between the black hole X-ray binary and the binary black hole populations shows that there is a diversity of formation mechanisms.<\/jats:p><jats:p>Given the array of new electromagnetic and gravitational wave capabilities currently being planned, the future of black hole spin studies is bright.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1146\/annurev-astro-112420-035022","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2021,6,11]],"date-time":"2021-06-11T19:20:14Z","timestamp":1623439214000},"page":"117-154","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":280,"title":["Observational Constraints on Black Hole Spin"],"prefix":"10.1146","volume":"59","author":[{"given":"Christopher S.","family":"Reynolds","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Institute of Astronomy, University of Cambridge, Cambridge CB3 OHA, United Kingdom;"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"22","reference":[{"key":"B1","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","DOI":"10.1103\/PhysRevLett.116.061102"},{"key":"B2","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","DOI":"10.1103\/PhysRevLett.116.241103"},{"key":"B3","first-page":"031040","volume":"9","author":"Abbott BP","year":"2019","journal-title":"Phys.
